transcript:
User: Hi — I saw your ad on Facebook about answering missed calls. I keep losing patients after hours, so I'm curious how it works.
Agent: Got it, you saw us on Facebook and you’re losing patients after hours — that’s exactly what we help with.  

So when someone calls after you’re closed right now, what actually happens — does it just ring out or hit voicemail?
User: Right now, calls after hours hit voicemail, and we miss booking about 20 potential appointments a week.
Agent: Yeah, that’s a lot of appointments slipping away when it just goes to voicemail.  

So roughly how busy are your phones during the day — is it mostly under control then, or are you missing daytime calls too?
User: During the day it's manageable, but after-hours is our main issue. That's when we lose most calls.
Agent: Makes sense, that lines up with what we hear from a lot of practices.  

Those after-hours calls that hit voicemail — do people usually leave a message, or do they just hang up and call the next office?
User: Most hang up and probably call the next office. That's why I worry about losing them to competitors.
Agent: Yeah, that’s exactly the risk — they’re not just “missed calls,” they’re new patients choosing someone else.  

Has anyone ever walked you through what that could be costing you each week in lost appointments, using your own numbers?
User: No, not really. I've only estimated that about half would book if someone answered, with appointments averaging $650.
Agent: Got it, that helps — let’s use your numbers then.  

If you’re missing about 20 potential appointments a week, and even half would book at $650, that’s roughly $6,500 slipping away every week… and over a month, about $28,100 — does that feel in the ballpark for what you’re seeing?
User: Yes, that sounds accurate and is exactly why I'm interested in a service like this.
Agent: Yeah, totally get why you’re looking at this then — that’s real money walking out the door every month.  

So… the next step is simple: it’s a 20‑minute walkthrough where we plug in your numbers and show exactly how we stop those after‑hours calls from slipping to competitors — what’s better for you, later today or tomorrow?
User: Tomorrow works for me. Let's go ahead and book the live call for then.
Agent: Awesome, we can definitely set that up for tomorrow.  

To get you booked in, what’s your first name?
User: My name is Maria Gonzales.
Agent: Nice to meet you, Maria.  

Got it — and what’s the name of your practice or company?
User: The name of my practice is Bright Smile Dental.
Agent: Bright Smile Dental — got it, thanks.  

Quick check — you’re on Central time, right?
User: Yes, I'm in Central Time, America/Chicago.
Agent: Got it, perfect, we’ll keep everything in Central.  

Soonest I can get you in is Wednesday at 7:15 pm Central, or Thursday at 10:00 am Central — which of those works better for you?
User: Let's book the live call for Wednesday at 7:15 pm Central.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that for you.
Agent: Maria, you’re all set — we’ve got you booked for Wednesday at 7:15 pm Central with Jay. You’ll get a text in a moment with all the details, and you can reschedule from that link if something comes up.

Is there anything else I can help you with before we hop off?

…Alright, really glad you called today. Jay’s looking forward to meeting you and walking through how to stop those after‑hours calls from slipping away. Have a great rest of your day — bye!
